records.last_location: Ch7 - The Dynamics of Your Inner Earth
records.text: Nature does not hurry, yet everything is accomplished.
records.work: recoverable ancestor: Archie J. Bahm's 1958 translation of Tao Te Ching 73 - 'IT does not hurry; yet everything is accomplished'
records.editorial_status: REMOVE, not reframe. The word that made this perfect for Earth - 'Nature', substituted for 'It' - is exactly the host-aligned alteration. Restoring the ancestor weakens the Earth-specific resonance; keeping 'Nature' asks Lao Tzu to say something the source does not. Unlike Plutarch it would also inherit a modern-translation rights problem, so the line is not worth rescuing. If the section needs the idea of unhurried unfolding, the chapter can make that observation itself.
records.notes: Audit: EVOLVED APHORISM / RECOVERABLE ANCESTOR. Two findings inside one line: the circulating form substitutes 'Nature' for 'It', and the ancestor is a specific modern translation rather than the Chinese text.
